verdict.rationale: Missive's first-party MCP integration docs say users can add a "Custom MCP" by entering a server URL and choosing an auth method (none, bearer token, or OAuth 2.0). Any MCP-compatible server then becomes available to Missive's AI assistant, which also ships with ready-made MCP integrations for Notion, Linear, and Attio. Missive's own MCP server, which lets external AI apps connect to it, is a separate capability and is not credited here. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that custom MCP servers' tools work reliably in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: With custom MCP, you can connect any MCP-compatible server to Missive's AI Copilot and let AI interact with your internal systems, proprietary data, or homegrown tools.
Add "Custom MCP" and enter a name and your server URL. Choose an authentication method and click Add
Choose an authentication method (none, bearer token, or OAuth 2.0, with custom scopes if your provider needs them) and click Add
Missive ships with ready-to-use MCP integrations for Notion, Linear, and Attio, plus AI automation platforms like Lindy.ai.
